title: Audit change record schema and actor identity linking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a unified audit event shape for RBAC v2 admin/control actions that links SSO/SAML identity assertions to actor records, captures compact diffs of target state mutations, and supports downstream indexing/querying, retention/redaction policies, and regression-safe rollouts.
problem_statement: Current audit logs are inconsistent across services: actor identity tone varies (email vs internal_id), SAML/OIDC assertions are sometimes omitted, target diffs are stored as blobs without path-level indexing, and admin actions lack atomicity metadata. This complicates investigations, makes retention/redaction error-prone, and blocks efficient alerting for privilege escalations.
proposal_summary: Introduce an Audit Change Record (ACR) event shape with explicit actor_assertion fields (saml_oidc), an actor_enrichment step that resolves to a stable actor_reference, a compact path-value diff encoding for target mutations, and standard metadata for atomicity, provenance, and storage classification. Provide a migration path for producers and a compatibility adapter for older consumers.
schema_fields: event_id: stable UUID (v4) as string
type: string enumerated (admin.change | admin.permission_change | system.config_update | user.role_assignment)
occurred_at: ISO-8601 timestamp in UTC
actor_assertion: string (raw SAML/OIDC assertion fingerprint or token reference)
actor_reference: string (internal canonical id, e.g., user:id or service:id)
actor_identity_hints: comma-separated list (email, saml_nameid, external_id)
actor_confidence_score: integer 0-100 (derived from SSO mapping heuristics)
session_id: tracing session id carried from front-end auth
request_trace_id: tracing id for distributed traces
target: string (resource canonical path e.g., org/123/team/ops/user/789)
target_type: string (user, role, policy, org, project)
change_set_encoding: string (compact-patch-v1)
changes: list of path:before->after strings encoded as compact-patch entries
change_type: string (modify | create | delete | permission_grant | permission_revoke)
atomicity_group: string (optional id for grouped mutations)
provenance: string (producer service id + version)
audit_version: string (schema version, e.g., 2025-02-acr-v1)
retention_class: string (ephemeral | standard | pii-sensitive)
redaction_mask_policy: string (none | mask-emails | redact-assertions)
index_keys: csv (actor_reference, target, target_type, change_type, auth_method)
auth_method: string (saml | oidc | api_key | internal)
user_visible_summary: short human readable string used in console timelines
encoding_and_diff_format: compact-patch-v1: an ordered list of path-value pairs where each entry is encoded as path|op|before|after (pipe-delimited). Example: 'members[2].role|replace|member|admin'
Rationale: path-level entries avoid full JSON blobs, admit efficient path-indexing, and minimize sensitive data retention by allowing per-path redaction rules
Large-blob fallback: for very large arrays or binary blobs, store a digest and pointer to offstore blob (S3) with separate retention controls
Atomicity: atomicity_group groups multiple events into a single logical transaction; consumers can apply-or-rollback by grouping event_ids
actor_linking_and_enrichment: Producers must attach actor_assertion when available (SAML/OIDC assertion fingerprint or token reference)
Enrichment service resolves assertion -> actor_reference using mapping tables and recent SSO assertion cache
Store actor_identity_hints to surface ambiguous mappings (e.g., two matching emails across directories)
actor_confidence_score computed from (assertion freshness, email verified, directory_match) used by console to flag low-confidence audit entries
For short-lived service tokens, store service:id and mark auth_method=internal or api_key as applicable
retention_and_redaction_guidelines: Default standard retention: 365 days for standard events
PII-sensitive classification: events that contain emails, phone numbers, or raw assertions => retention_class=pii-sensitive, default retention 90 days and strict redaction
Redaction rules applied at path-level: compact-patch entries referencing paths matching /email or /assertion are replaced with masked values according to redaction_mask_policy
Retention enforcement: index pruning must respect retention_class and should remove searchable index entries before blob removal to avoid accidental reconstitution
Legal-hold: provide override metadata (legal_hold_id) to extend retention per event (implemented as index flag)
Sampling: high-volume low-sensitivity events may be sampled; sampled events must still record a sampled=true flag and a sketch of changes (hash) for forensic linkage
storage_and_indexing: Primary store: append-only audit event store (immutable) partitioned by occurred_at month and org id
Secondary index: columnar index for fast queries on actor_reference, target, change_type, and auth_method
Search index: tokenized user_visible_summary + target path for console timelines
Offstore attachments: large blobs and raw assertions stored encrypted in offstore with pointer in event (attachment_uri)
Retention GC pipeline first removes searchable index entries then flags offstore blobs for deletion after delay to allow replication consistency
query_and_alerting_patterns: Common queries: find all changes to a given role in last 30 days; list all revocations performed by an external admin; surface low-confidence mapping events for review
Alerting rules: privilege_grant to highly_sensitive_role by actor_confidence_score < 70 => immediate pager with event_id and session_id
Watchlist: attach customer-provided watchlist to index to allow near-real-time notifications on matching target paths
Sampling considerations: when sampling is in effect, alerts must reference both live stream and sampled store to avoid false negatives
compatibility_migration_plan: Phase 0: publish schema docs and a lightweight producer SDK that emits ACR with fallbacks when actor_assertion is absent
Phase 1: Roll producers behind feature flag; enable enrichment service to backfill actor_reference for new events
Phase 2: Deploy compatibility adapter that can translate legacy blob events to compact-patch approximations for query tooling
Phase 3: Switch console to prefer actor_reference and compact changes; deprecate legacy fields after 90 days of stable ingestion metrics
acceptance_criteria: Schema published in docs site and internal protobuf/avro spec available
Producer SDK implemented with examples in at least 3 services (auth-service, admin-api, console)
Enrichment service can resolve >99% of assertions to actor_reference in CI tests
Alerting rule demo: create low-confidence privilege grant and verify pager triggers in staging
Migration adapter able to translate 95% of sampled legacy events into compact-patch entries for search
rollout_steps: Design review with Security and Privacy (week 0)
Implement producer SDK and enrichment service (week 1-3)
Instrument 3 pilot producers and validate event volumes and index size (week 4)
Enable retention/redaction hooks and run simulated GC to validate no data loss (week 5)
Full rollout and deprecation of legacy fields (week 7-10)
